newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged amid new supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged amid new supply.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices held steady in extremely quiet secondary action Tuesday, as several of the week's largest new issues priced.

One market analyst said that despite the flat secondary, the day's new issues were priced aggressively. "I couldn't believe the secondary was just sitting there with the new issue pricing so strong," the analyst said.

Underwriters repriced several of the day's largest new issues, including Jefferson County, Ala.'s $261 million sewer bond deal. Raymond James & Associates Inc said it lowered yields in several maturities.

BancAmerica Securities won the largest competitive issue of the day, a $143 million Industry Urban Development Agency, Calif. deal reoffered at a 5.25 percent yield in 2012. The offering is insured by MBIA Insurance Corp.
Despite several large new issues Tuesday, upcoming supply remains thin. The Blue List of upcoming supply remained below $1 billion Tuesday, falling to $938 million from $958 million on Monday.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales for Wednesday are expected to total $993 million in 23 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Competitive sales total $125 million in seven sales. The largest is a $70 million Knox County, Tenn., deal at 1000 EST. Negotiated sales total $868 million in 16 offerings. The largest is a $264 million Harris County Health Facilities Authority, Texas, issue through Smith Barney Inc.
The U.S. Treasury is scheduled to sell $12 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday.
In the municipal secondary market Tuesday, bids on Dade County, Fla., water and sewer FGIC 5-1/4s of 2026 were down one basis point from Monday at 5.63 percent net.
Houston water and sewer system 5-3/8s of 2027 were bid at 5.70 percent net, also down one basis point.
The Treasury market, meanwhile, was also mostly flat heading into the New York close. The long bond was unchanged at 97-12/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
